st-boar-firstaid-en-001.text:
The offline source doesn't give first-aid steps for this. In an emergency, call your local emergency number. What the source says:
Open Chest Wounds > Treatment > Making a flutter valve: Get some sort of plastic that is bigger than the wound. Ideas: credit card or similar, Ziploc bag, some first aid kits will have a ready-to-use valve. Tape the plastic patch over the wound on only 3 sides. The 4th side is left open, allowing blood to drain and air to escape. This opening should be at the bottom (as determined by the victim’s position). When the casualty inhales, the bag will be sucked in, but when the casualty exhales, the air will exit through the untaped side. [1]

st-boar-firstaid-en-002.text:
From the offline source:
External Chest Compressions: - · Compression Depth: Press down firmly and smoothly. For adults, compress the chest at least two inches (five centimeters) deep. For infants or children, compress the chest about one-third to one- half of its depth. - · Compression Rate: Perform compressions at a rate of 100 to 120 compressions per minute. This equates to about two compressions per second. - · Complete Chest Recoil: Allow the chest to fully recoil between each compression, without lifting your hands off the chest. This allows the heart to refill with blood. [1]

In an emergency, call your local emergency number (911 in the US, 112 in Europe).

st-boar-firstaid-en-004.text:
From the offline source:
Management > Rewarming: Rewarming shock (or rewarming collapse) is a sudden drop in blood pressure in combination with a low cardiac output which may occur during active treatment of a severely hypothermic person. There was a theoretical concern that external rewarming rather than internal rewarming may increase the risk. These concerns were partly believed to be due to afterdrop, a situation detected during laboratory experiments where there is a continued decrease in core temperature after rewarming has been started. Recent studies have not supported these concerns, and problems are not found with active external rewarming. [1]

Be Safe AFTER: - Listen to local alerts and authorities for information on areas to avoid and shelter locations. - Save phone calls for emergencies. Phone systems often are down or busy after a disaster. Use text messages or social media to communicate with family and friends. - Avoid wading in floodwater, which can contain dangerous debris. Water may be deeper than it appears. - Be aware of the risk of electrocution. Underground or downed power lines can electrically charge water. Do not touch electrical equipment if it is wet or if you are standing in water. - Stay away from damaged buildings, roads and bridges. [1]

st-boar-medlineplus-en-015.text:
Head injury: if they might have hurt their neck (a fall from height, a high-speed hit) or aren't responding, don't move them unless they're in danger; support the head so the head, neck and spine stay in a straight line. If they're not responding and not breathing normally, call emergency services and start CPR. If they're not responding but breathing normally, and they're vomiting or their breathing sounds blocked or gurgling, turn them on their side, keeping the head and spine in line. For a bump, hold an ice pack or frozen peas wrapped in a tea towel on it for short periods; never put ice directly on the skin. An adult should stay with them for the first 24 hours. They should rest, avoid alcohol until they feel better, and avoid contact sport for 3 weeks. Get urgent medical advice if they've been sick once, feel dizzy, take blood thinners, or had been drinking; if told to go to hospital, don't drive yourself. Call emergency services if they were knocked out and haven't woken, can't stay awake, have a seizure, vomit more than once, fell more than 1 metre or 5 stairs, were hit at high speed, have problems seeing, hearing, speaking, walking or with balance, new weakness or numbness, clear fluid from the ears or nose, bleeding from the ears, or changed behaviour.

Source: St John Ambulance (UK), Spinal injury; St John Ambulance (UK), Head injury; St John Ambulance (UK), CPR; British Heart Foundation, How to do CPR; St John Ambulance (UK), Recovery position; NHS, Head injury and concussion; British Red Cross, Head injury; healthdirect (AU), Head injuries. st-boar-simplewiki-en-001.text: Heat naturally flows from hotter objects to colder objects because this process results in a decrease in the total entropy of the system, which is consistent with the second law of thermodynamics, though the context provided focuses on the first law. Clausius defined energy as a state function related to work exchanged during adiabatic processes [2], and the context does not specify Kelvin's phrasing regarding this principle.

st-boar-simplewiki-en-002.text: The Standard Model is incomplete because it does not include a full theory of gravitation, fails to explain the accelerating expansion of the universe, and does not contain a particle for dark matter [2]. Physicists are working on extensions to the Standard Model to incorporate gravity and address these cosmological mysteries.

st-boar-simplewiki-en-003.text: Cosmology is the study of the universe's structure and changes, whereas cosmogony specifically studies the origin of the universe, such as the Big Bang theory [3, 5]. Science cannot yet describe the earliest moments of the universe because there is currently no testable theory of quantum gravity to explain the Planck time [1].

st-boar-simplewiki-en-004.text: In classical mechanics, one joule is defined as the energy transferred to an object when a force of one newton is exerted over a distance of one meter [1]. The watt is a unit of power, and since power is work divided by time, a joule relates to power and time via the equation Power = Work $\div$ Time [3].

st-boar-simplewiki-en-005.text: The Atacama Desert receives very little rain because mountains to the east and the ocean to the west create a rain shadow, preventing moisture from reaching the inland area [1]. People in Chile have developed methods to collect water from fog, as moisture condenses on surfaces and drips into pans for drinking and crops [1].

st-boar-simplewiki-en-006.text: Forecasters found Hurricane Vince surprising because it formed in waters thought to be too cold for tropical or subtropical cyclones to exist [2]. Despite its unusual nature, the storm did drop rain on the Iberian Peninsula in Spain [1].

st-boar-simplewiki-en-007.text: A Viking raid on Lindisfarne in 793 terrified the Christian West, during which the Vikings tore off the Gospels' bejeweled cover and raided Jarrow [4]. The monks fled the island, taking with them the body of St Cuthbert, which was later buried at Durham Cathedral [3].

st-boar-simplewiki-en-008.text: The English government initiated the Plantation of Ulster starting in the early 17th century to colonize the region and stop local resistance against English rule [2]. Settlers were sent from Scotland and England to establish control over the area [2].

st-boar-simplewiki-en-009.text: The Fatimid Caliphate ended in 1171, as the dynasty concluded with the reign of the last Caliph, Al-'Āḍid [3]. While the context does not detail the specific events leading to the end, it mentions the Fatimid dynasty ruling from 909 to 1171 [3].

st-boar-simplewiki-en-010.text: Banks manipulated the Libor rate by falsely changing interest rates before submission to profit from trades and to appear more creditworthy [4]. In response, the British Bankers' Association transferred oversight of Libor to UK regulators, and reforms mandated that banks base their submissions on actual inter-bank deposit market transactions [2]. Furthermore, the Financial Services Act 2012 brought Libor under UK regulatory oversight and created criminal offenses for making false statements [5].

st-boar-simplewiki-en-011.text: The shell shapes of Galápagos tortoises varied based on the local environment; those on humid highlands had domed shells, while those in dry lowlands had "saddleback" shells [3]. This variation in morphology across islands provided the physical evidence Darwin used to support his theory of evolution by natural selection [1, 4].

st-boar-simplewiki-en-012.text: Humans carry far more microorganisms than human cells, with the gut alone harboring about ten times as many microbes as human cells [1]. While some bacteria cause diseases, many are beneficial, helping with everyday activities like digesting food [2].

st-boar-simplewiki-en-014.text: The Manchester Metrolink system was established when Manchester became the first city in the UK to introduce a new tram system in 1992 [5]. Since then, the network has expanded significantly, growing from 37 km to 97 km with 99 stops [4]. Further extensions are being planned to double the network's size by 2040 [4].

st-boar-simplewiki-en-015.text: The name "Google" is a play on the word googol, referencing a number with one followed by one hundred zeroes [4]. Google earns money by advertising; it makes money when people or companies pay Google to show advertisements to people it thinks will click on them [2].
